   C. 2020 CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODE BIENNIAL UPDATE

  Under the Political Reform Act, public agencies are required to adopt a
  conflict of interest code designating positions required to file Statements of
  Economic Interests (Form 700), and assigning disclosure categories specifying
  the types of interests to be reported. The conflict of interest code must be
  reviewed every two years so that amendments may be made as needed.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-43 entitled,
  “A Resolution of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California,
  Amending the City of San Gabriel Conflict of Interest Code and Rescinding
  Resolution No. 18-46.”

  D. SAN GABRIEL VALLEY REGIONAL HOUSING TRUST – AFFILIATE
  MEMBERSHIP

  With the passage of SB 751 (Rubio), cities in the San Gabriel Valley and the
  County of Los Angeles have the ability to form the San Gabriel Valley Regional
  Trust (SGVRHT) Joint Powers Authority (JPA). The Trust is intended to provide
  a stronger opportunity for San Gabriel Valley cities to attract and secure
  funding for supportive housing and affordable housing projects. In April 2020,
  staff provided a detailed staff report to the City Council regarding the
  formation of the San Gabriel Valley Regional Trust and at this time would like
  to pursue an affiliate membership at a cost of $3,000 a year.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Receive and file the information contained in this staff report; and
  2. Approve Resolution No. 20-44 which appropriates funding for this
  membership.

  E. LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL CONFERENCE RESOLUTIONS

  The League of California Cities (League) will hold their virtual Annual
  Conference on October 7-9, 2020. This year, the League will vote on the
  resolution regarding the General Assembly of the League of California Cities
  Calling for an Amendment of Section 230 of the Communications Decency

   Act of 1996 to Require Social Media Companies to Remove Materials Which
  Promote Criminal Activity.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the League’s proposed
  resolution and approve the voting delegate and voting alternate to use their
  discretion to vote on the proposed resolution.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND THE SAN
  GABRIEL CHAMBER OF COMMERCE FOR BUSINESS, ECONOMIC AND
  CIVIC PROMOTION SERVICES, IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $31,680

  On June 2, 2020, as part of a larger discussion regarding the City’s budget and
  annual memberships to partnering agencies, the topic of the City’s financial
  support of the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce was raised. Historically, the
  relationship between the City of San Gabriel and the San Gabriel Chamber of
  Commerce has been maintained through the shared goals and efforts of
  assisting, promoting and supporting San Gabriel businesses. The item under
  consideration formalizes that relationship and the financial support therein
  and establishes agreed deliverables by the Chamber to the City pursuant to
  an agreement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss and consider the following
  actions:

  1. Continue exploring formalizing an agreement with the San Gabriel
  Chamber of Commerce for Business, Economic and Civic Promotion
  Services through June 30, 2021; or
  2. Approve counter proposal by the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce for
  a Presidential Circle Membership for Fiscal Year 2020-2021; or
  3. Redirect funding to general Economic Development account and do not
  proceed with an agreement with the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 1, 2020  4
   B. CARES ACT FUNDING

  The CARES Act established the $150 billion Coronavirus Relief Fund which
  provides for payments to State and local entities. The Federal government has
  established guidelines for the receiving and expending of such funds. As part
  of its Fiscal Year 2020-21 budget, the State of California allocated funds to
  ever city in the state on a population basis. The City of San Gabriel is slated
  to receive $495,000 in total by October 2020. This report details the City’s plan
  for use of the funds.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 20-45 which
  formalizes the receipt of CARES Act revenue and appropriates funding for
  equipment usage and emergency provision.

  C. FIFTH AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT
  WITH ATHENS

  The City of San Gabriel and Athens Services is considering an amendment to
  the existing agreement with Athens Services allowing Athens to implement
  new rates to comply with current state mandated organics policies for
  commercial and multi-family accounts and extend the renewing contract term
  in exchange for annual payments to the City.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approves the Fifth Amendment to the
  Amended and Restated Agreement, the new rate adjustment, and the 14-year
  increase to our current 11-year contract.

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 1, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:31 P.M. on Tuesday, September 1, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating
by teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Ding.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chief City Clerk Clark announced that staff had requested that item 4B, Material
  Demands, be pulled from the agenda to be considered at the next regular meeting
  instead, due to a technical error in which the online version of the agenda materials
  for this item displayed the August 18, 2020, staff report and attachments instead of
  the September 1, 2020, staff report and attachments.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca to approve
  the agenda order as amended to remove Item 4B.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  September 1, 2020
   ABSENT:  NONE

2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  The presentation was made by Fire Chief Wallace; Police Chief Harris; Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Chaparyan; and Vice Mayor Liao and
  Council Member Ding, as members of the 10-Point Plan for Recovery, Resiliency,
  and Reinvestment subcommittee.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Norma Alejo, Co-owner/Operations Manager of Navarro’s Towing, provided
  comments expressing dissatisfaction with the Request for Proposals (RFP) process for
  RFP 2020-07, Franchise Agreement for Tow Truck Services.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Council Member Pu, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A and 4C – 4E as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A and 4C – 4E as presented by a vote of 5-0
  as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of August 18, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of August 18, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This item was removed from the agenda, to be considered at the September 15,
  2020, regular City Council meeting.

  C. 2020 CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODE BIENNIAL UPDATE

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-43 entitled, “A Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Amending the City of San Gabriel
  Conflict of Interest Code and Rescinding Resolution No. 18-46.”

  D. SAN GABRIEL VALLEY REGIONAL HOUSING TRUST – AFFILIATE MEMBERSHIP

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-44 appropriating funding for the
  membership.

  E. LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL CONFERENCE RESOLUTIONS

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  September 1, 2020
   The City Council received and filed the League’s proposed resolution, and
  approved the voting delegate and voting alternate to use their discretion to vote
  on the proposed resolution.

5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND THE SAN GABRIEL
  CHAMBER OF COMMERCE FOR BUSINESS, ECONOMIC AND CIVIC
  PROMOTION SERVICES, IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $31,680

  The staff presentation was made by Economic Development Manager Domenica
  Megerdichian.

  The following provided comments in opposition to an agreement: Douglas Richter;
  Cheri Cabot; George Valdez; and Sean McMorris, resident.

  The following provided comments in favor of the City accepting the Chamber’s
  Presidential Circle Membership: Sandy Rosco, Executive Director, San Gabriel
  Chamber of Commerce.

  The following provided comments in favor of a formal agreement: Dr. Jennings-
  Nuñez; and Jeanne E. Raya, CRM, John L. Raya Insurance Group, San Gabriel.

  City Attorney Lemieux explained that Council Member Ding had contacted him
  regarding a potential conflict of interest on this item as the Council Member is a
  member of the Chamber of Commerce. After review, it was determined that
  Council Member Ding has a statutory non-interest in the matter and therefore may
  fully participate. City Attorney Lemieux disclosed this information at the request of
  Council Member Ding in the interest of transparency.

  Discussion included that the Chamber of Commerce (Chamber) is a membership
  agency rather than a contract service; value to member businesses; lack of
  Chamber outreach to some businesses and language-barrier challenges; Chamber
  support of City events; requested deliverables are reasonable; whether more
  negotiation would be productive; preference for direct assistance to the
  community; suggestion for the Chamber to add multi-lingual staff to facilitate
  outreach to business owners whose first language is not English; having City
  personnel on the Chamber Board of Directors; reasonable metrics in the
  agreement; possible option for the City to have a regular membership and engage
  the Chamber additionally on a project-by-project basis; dollar-value for
  deliverables; not using non-Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds
  for grants to businesses; the difference between the Chamber and other quasi-
  governmental joint powers authorities; and the option of having in-house
  Economic Development staff or other contractors provide the deliverables in the
  agreement instead of the Chamber.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Council Member Harrington,
  to continue exploring formalizing an agreement with the San Gabriel Chamber of
  Commerce for Business, Economic and Civic Promotion Services through June 30,
  2021.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  September 1, 2020
   ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. CARES ACT FUNDING
  The staff presentation was made by Interim Finance Director Ken Louie.

  Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nuñez provided comments requesting that funds be used to
  directly benefit the City’s residents secondary to COVID hardships, rather than for
  City technology.

  Discussion included seniors receiving meals from sources other than the City;
  support for the senior meal program and relief grants to businesses; support for a
  contingency fund; restrictions for use of CARES ACT funds; COVID-19-related rental
  assistance; funding and reasons for requested technology items; and support for
  the purchase of a City phone system.

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Council Member Harrington, to
  adopt Resolution No. 20-45 which formalizes the receipt of CARES Act revenue
  and appropriates funding, as amended to allocate $50,000 for a City phone system
  and $40,000 for the senior meal program through the end of the year, with the
  remainder of the funding to be brought back to the City Council for discussion,
  with the intention that it be used for various forms of assistance for the community.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  C. FIFTH AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT WITH
  ATHENS

  The staff presentation was made by Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de
  Vinck.

  The following provided comments in favor of the Amendment: Sandy Rosco,
  Executive Director, San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce; Terri Huerta, resident and
  Mission San Gabriel employee; and Alexis Salamanca, President, Board of Directors,
  San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce.

  Discussion included appreciation for the work involved in working out the
  amendment; desire for renewal incentive monies to be spent on street paving;
  timing for implementing rate increases; ways Athens is assisting commercial
  customers with COVID-19-related challenges; road impact fees; compliance with
  recycling legislation; and organics recycling.

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Harrington, to
  approve the Fifth Amendment to the Amended and Restated Agreement, the new
  rate adjustment, and the 14-year increase to the City’s current 11-year contract.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

7. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  September 1, 2020
 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto reminded the community to please follow social-distancing protocols
  during the Labor Day holiday weekend.

9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Liao reported on his participation in a Census 2020 caravan.

  Council Member Pu reported on activities of the ad hoc subcommittee for the Human
  Equity, Access, and Relations (HEAR) Commission, San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing
  Trust, and the Council of Governments (COG) Transportation Committee.

  Council Member Ding thanked staff for their hard work on the agenda, and
  encouraged the community to complete the Census and to stay home on the long
  weekend.

10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

11. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Menchaca reminded everyone to take COVID-19 safety precautions on the
  Labor Day weekend. She adjourned the meeting at 9:37 P.M.
